claims.text: The as-synthesized high-entropy alloy has high configurational or chemical disorder.
The superconducting behavior of the as-synthesized alloy is uncharacterized.
Controlled thermal annealing can incrementally increase local chemical order without changing the alloy's overall composition.
Increasing local atomic order increases electron-phonon coupling efficiency.
Increasing local atomic order reduces excessive electron scattering.
Increasing local atomic order optimizes electron-phonon interaction pathways.
Reduced scattering and optimized electron-phonon interactions promote more effective Cooper-pair formation.
Annealing-induced local order will raise the superconducting transition temperature relative to the unannealed baseline.
Annealing-induced local order will produce a sharper, narrower superconducting transition relative to the unannealed baseline.
Annealing may increase the critical magnetic fields relative to the unannealed baseline.
The proposed effect is expected only for moderate annealing that improves local order without causing phase separation or composition changes.
The magnitude of the Tc enhancement and transition sharpening depends on annealing parameters and the resulting degree of local order.
Annealed and unannealed samples should be drawn from the same initial alloy batch and tested under identical low-temperature measurement settings.
Resistivity and magnetization measurements can be used to assess Tc and superconducting transition characteristics.
